messages.author: 12f269733c6eb9a2
messages.subject: Re: Problem running Uniform key models for trapping webs
parts:
Carolyn:

Here is my suspicion about your analysis. When fitting the uniform key with any
sort of adjustments to trapping web data, there exists the possibility that no
adjustment terms are necessary to fit your data. That results in a fitted
model that fits a horizontal detection function (no diminution in detectability
as you move out on the rings of your web). In this situation, p is estimated to
be 1 for all rings; there are no parameters being estimated because p=1 at the
centre of the the web (by assumption). Without parameters being estimated,
there is no uncertainty associated with the density or abundance estimates.

This only arises for the uniform key, because the half normal (negative
exponential is not a good key function to use, and you should not really
consider its use) and hazard rate key functions have a decreasing detection
function as a characteristic of the key function. The decrease in
detectability when using the uniform as the key function comes as a result of
the adjustment terms (which are used/not used as a result of AIC model
selection by Distance default).

The emphasis is not really on the fitting or behaviour of the detection function
fitting, but rather your data. It is not unlikely with trapping web data that
you have edge effects with large numbers of captures in our outer ring(s). As
a result, the fitting algorithm believes that detectability does not drop with
distance from web centre, but actually might be increasing with distance from
centre. However, Distance has constraints that will not allow detection
functions to increase with distance, so the compromise seen with the uniform
key function is to make the detection function flat. The estimate of abundance
is then equal to the number of captures, because detectability is estimated to
be perfect. This is probably the fault of the edge effects which are a symptom
of trapping webs.

messages.author: 4b4a7b00c1dd09c7
messages.subject: Re: Problem running Uniform key models for trapping webs
parts:
Carolyn, (list)

I agree with Eric re uniform+no adjustments, likely caused by edge effects.

If you marked trapped animals, and recorded recaptures, you may want to
use the Spatially Explicit Capture Recapture framework for analysis
instead. You can analyze the data using the software Density
http://www.otago.ac.nz/density/
(references are also on that web site) or WinBUGS (code and book
reference at
http://www.mbr-pwrc.usgs.gov/pubanalysis/roylebook/
). Takes a bit of work to properly understand this alternative
framework, however.

Hope this helps,

- Len

--
